question: Deterministic radiation effects (such as radiation burns) have a threshold dose below which they do not occur, unlike stochastic effects which follow a no-threshold model.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. Deterministic effects (epilation, erythema, radiation burns) have a threshold — they only occur above a certain dose. Stochastic effects (carcinogenesis) are modelled as having no threshold: even small doses carry a small probability of harm.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Deterministic effects occur only above a threshold dose and increase in severity with dose; stochastic effects (cancer, hereditary changes) follow a no-threshold linear model — any dose carries some probability of harm.
